title: SAFe and LeSS: agile across several teams

videos.script: Scrum describes one team. Kanban describes one board. Most software that matters is built by many teams. {{many}} Six people have fifteen pairs who may need to talk. Twelve people have sixty-six. {{pairs}} So organisations split into teams, and a new cost appears: one team waiting for another. {{waiting}} There are two ways to answer it. Add coordination: shared planning, shared cadence, roles that manage the dependencies. That is SAFe. {{safe}} Or remove the need for coordination: one backlog, one product owner, teams that can finish a feature on their own. That is LeSS. {{less}} This lesson takes both seriously, looks at the two days SAFe is famous for, and ends with three questions to ask before scaling anything. {{questions}}
